translations.answer: In the OmniH2O report's Unitree H1, 19-DoF, 50 Hz strategy setup, 25-step body perception combined with previous action history through DAgger teacher-student distillation allows for implicit global linear velocity input; it outperforms the VIO, MLP, and GRU speed input variants in a real-robot standing-motion evaluation of 20 sequences, but this conclusion cannot be directly extrapolated to other robots, sensors, or dynamic actions.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The policy receives reliable joint position, joint velocity, base angular velocity, projected gravity, and previous actions.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: The motion goal is a sparse three-point head-and-hands kinematic target.
translations.applicability.assumptions.2: Training uses a privileged teacher and DAgger-style action supervision in simulation.
translations.applicability.robots.0: Unitree H1 research platform in the OmniH2O setup
translations.applicability.simulators.0: Isaac Gym / PhysX in the official implementation
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper reports a controlled simulation ablation and a real-robot comparison, and the official commit exposes the corresponding history and DAgger implementation. Confidence is capped because the real-world quantitative set contains only 20 standing motions, broader demonstrations are mainly qualitative, and no independent cross-robot replication is included.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Section 3 (student state and policy distillation), Table 1(a,b,d), and Table 2(a,b)
translations.evidence.0.note: Supports the no-global-linear-velocity design, 25-step history, DAgger ablation, and reported real-robot comparison.
